hero.subtitle: Prevent shock hazards during wet floor cleaning, eliminate kitchen downtime, and audit kilowatt costs per appliance.

problems.title: Water, heat and high-load circuits share the same few square meters.
problems.intro: Fast-food kitchens run some of the most electrically demanding operations in retail, yet most stores have no live view of what happens inside their breaker panels.

electrocution.title: Electrocution risk during night mopping
electrocution.body: Crews mop and hose floors around fryers, grills and panels with no way of knowing whether a circuit is leaking current.
electrocution.consequence: Serious injuries to staff and direct legal liability for the store.

breakerTrips.title: Breaker trips in the middle of the rush
breakerTrips.body: Undetected faults build up until a breaker trips at lunch or dinner peak and takes a whole line down.
breakerTrips.consequence: Lost sales, wasted food and orders piling up.

energyWaste.title: Unmonitored equipment inflating the bill
energyWaste.body: One utility bill for the whole store and no visibility per appliance, so idle or failing equipment quietly drives costs up.
energyWaste.consequence: Higher energy bills every month with no clear cause.

audits.title: Labor audits and liability
audits.body: Without traceable electrical safety records, inspections by SUNAFIL and INDECI are hard to pass.
audits.consequence: Fines or a temporary store closure.

safety.title: Know a station is safe before anyone touches it.
safety.intro: Clear, touch-friendly signals at every station: early warnings when something changes and simple protocols for the moments that matter.

clean.title: Safe-to-Clean protocol
clean.body: One tap before the washdown. Each wet zone is checked for isolation and leakage, and the screen only gives the go-ahead when every zone passes. Every check is logged for audits.

alarm.title: Instant multi-sensory alarms
alarm.body: A ground fault turns the station screen red, sounds a buzzer and names the machine to avoid. The supervisor gets an SMS at the same moment.
alarm.headline: Step away
alarm.instruction: Do not touch the fryer bank or the surrounding floor.
alarm.note: The alarm fires before the breaker's 30 mA trip point, so the crew is warned first.

pause.title: 30-second cleaning pause
pause.body: Touch input locks for 30 seconds so greasy screens can be wiped without triggering anything. Safety alarms stay active the whole time.
pause.ended: Cleaning pause finished. Touch input is active again.

offline.title: When a sensor goes silent
offline.body: No data never means safe. If a sensor stops reporting, the machine is flagged as unmonitored and must be treated as energized.
offline.headline: Unmonitored equipment — Do not touch
offline.instruction: Treat it as energized until the signal returns.
offline.recommendation: Report it to your store manager so a certified technician can check the sensor.

management.title: Energy costs, incidents and compliance in one dashboard.
management.intro: See what every machine costs in soles, catch equipment left running after closing and keep maintenance on schedule with certified technicians.

costs.title: Cost per machine in soles
costs.body: Each circuit is metered separately and converted with your tariff, so you know which equipment drives the bill.

idle.title: Off-hours idle detection
idle.body: Load after closing is compared with the store schedule to flag equipment that should have been switched off.

sla.title: SLA-tracked maintenance
sla.body: Every fault opens an incident with an SLA clock and a work order for a certified technician.

continuity.title: Operational continuity
continuity.body: Early warnings let you fix faults off-peak instead of losing a line at rush hour.

management.ctaNote: Already a customer? Log in to see your stores.

dashboard.caption: Manager dashboard preview with sample data for one store.

threshold.title: Combi oven 01 · threshold not configured
threshold.body: Until someone confirms its limits, this machine runs on the safe default: an alarm at 30 mA of leakage. It stays protected and flagged in the dashboard.

ecosystem.title: From breaker panel to action in three steps.
ecosystem.intro: Sensors measure, the edge gateway decides locally, and software robots handle the follow-up.

clamps.title: Non-invasive clamp sensors
clamps.body: Split-core current, leakage and temperature clamps snap onto existing circuits in the breaker panel. No rewiring, no service interruption.

edge.title: Edge telemetry sync
edge.body: The gateway streams readings to the cloud in real time and keeps alarms, screens and logs working locally if the internet drops.

rpa.title: Automated RPA dispatch
rpa.body: Software robots open work orders, dispatch certified technicians and fall back to SMS when the primary channel fails.

measure.title: Measure
measure.body: Clamps sample current, leakage and temperature continuously.

evaluate.title: Evaluate
evaluate.body: The gateway compares each reading with the machine's threshold.

alert.title: Alert
alert.body: Station screens and buzzers react locally, without waiting for the cloud.

act.title: Act
act.body: The platform logs the event and RPA opens the work order.

offline.title: Fryer bank sensor · platform link lost
offline.body: Readings are stored temporarily on the edge gateway and uploaded automatically when the connection returns, so the record has no gaps. Local alarms keep working meanwhile.

footer.tagline: IoT electrical safety and energy intelligence for fast-food kitchens.
footer.disclaimer: ElectroLink monitoring complements, but does not replace, certified electrical installations, residual-current protection devices and the periodic inspections required by Peruvian regulations (OSINERGMIN, INDECI, SUNAFIL). Alarm thresholds must be validated by a licensed electrical engineer for each site.
